PullRequest.Title: refactor(sessions): move sessions list row renderers to sessionsListRenderers.ts
PullRequest.Body:

## Why
Move 3 of phase 2, which splits the 11.5k-line `sessionsList.ts` into smaller modules. Stacked on #349660. Row rendering moves into its own module, so that the flat list (move 5) can render rows without loading the list control.

## What changed
- New `sessionsListRenderers.ts` with these regions, byte for byte: Tree Delegate, Chat Item Renderer, Approval Row Content, Session Item Renderer, Section Header Renderer, Session Group Renderer, Show More Renderer, and Accessibility. It also gets the 23 small helpers and constants they use, such as `formatSessionListTime`, `getSessionRowStatus`, `renderSearchHint`, and `getSessionSectionIcon`.
- The only other edits: `export` added to 26 declarations that `sessionsList.ts` still uses, import lines updated in 13 files (tests included), and the moved blocks deleted from `sessionsList.ts`. The moved code reads `$` from an import of `dom.js`, which is the same function as `sessionsList.ts`'s `const $ = DOM.$`. Nothing is re-exported from `sessionsList.ts`.
- The new module imports `sessionsList.css` and `disclosure.css`, so rows keep their styles in modules that do not load `sessionsList.ts`.

## Scope
No behavior changes.

## Blast Radius
Module load order only. The moved code has no module-level side effects, the new module does not import `sessionsList.ts`, and there are no import cycles. The 96 moved `localize` calls now belong to `sessionsListRenderers`, so language packs pick them up at the next translation pass.

## Verification
- Move check (a TypeScript compiler API script): all 257 top-level declaration blocks are identical at base and head, apart from 26 added `export` keywords. The other 13 files changed only import declarations.
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `check-cyclic-dependencies`, and `oxlint` on the changed files all pass.
- Sessions list unit tests and the tests of its importers: 6,992 tests, the same count as base.
- Component fixtures `sessionsList`, `sessionsListNotification`, `sessionsInboxScope`, and `blockedSessionsList`: 346/346 screenshots identical to base.
- Bundled CSS for desktop, web, server-web, and mobile: 6/6 files byte-identical.
- Code OSS Agents window, base and head: every grouping mode, Find, a context menu, drag and drop, and the blocked-sessions list give the same rows. All 12 screenshots are pixel-identical, and no new console errors appear.

Details are in the first comment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents-window startup and onboarding/archive-tour helper imports
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation precedes constructing the sessions UI or using onboarding target identifiers. The extracted module defines classes/functions and small constants; it does not construct renderers, resolve sessions, or start timers at module scope. Service/model initialization remains at the existing first-use sites.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Evaluate the extracted renderer module and its existing dependencies, including the same sessionsList.css and disclosure.css module identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extracted module evaluation per module-loader context, not one per row or importer; repeated imports reuse module identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer declarations, constants, CSS, and renderer dependencies were loaded through the larger sessionsList.ts module. Helper-only importers formerly loaded that larger module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dependency evaluation is on the initial import path, but no heavyweight service operation is newly executed there.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Module dependency graph and cold module-loader state; onboarding identifiers are constant-cost string formatting for the selected session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal dependency-ordered module evaluation; no added asynchronous work or service-instantiation burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module identity is shared across the updated importers and sessionsList.ts. CSS imports use the same resolved paths. Interface-only imports introduce no runtime service creation. Warm imports do not recreate declarations or the empty guide set.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from inspection of the complete added module, deleted declarations, and all importer diffs: initialization and helper bodies retain their previous behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime startup or bundling measurements were performed; the cost of an additional module boundary is not quantified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No concrete performance regression. Extraction changes dependency structure without establishing additional expensive startup work or collection-scaled initialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, scroll, search, and expand/collapse the main sessions tree, including nested chats and section/group headers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing WorkbenchObjectTree construction and visible-row rendering run synchronously before paint. Row session-property resolution is started without awaiting it, so backend enrichment is not a new first-paint prerequisite. Search filtering, row-height calculations, grouping, and caller scheduling were not changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an extension-provided chat session item's lazy properties through $resolveChatSessionItem when the row is rendered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one initial resolution attempt per distinct rendered session resource in the model's resolution epoch; supported extension controllers additionally cache/coalesce promises per resource. Provider refresh can reset the model guard. No resolver RPC for unsupported controllers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical observeSession call in the deleted SessionItemRenderer.renderSession body, with the same service instance, resource key, and controller caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget from rendering; returned enrichment later updates observables.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read resolved-item metadata from the shared chat index, parsing stored JSON on a cold index cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getIndex queue entry per applicable resolved DTO; the index is parsed once per cold index-cache lifetime, and warm reads reuse the entries object rather than reparsing per row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same transitive metadata call and globally sequenced, cached index lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after resolver completion; it delays the enrichment result, not a newly introduced synchronous rendering step.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible session/chat templates and distinct resources encountered while scrolling; header status scans scale with section/subtree session counts, and file-stat aggregation scales with the existing changes arrays.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Row DOM work is synchronous on the UI thread. Different resource resolutions can proceed concurrently, while same-resource calls are coalesced. Metadata index operations share ChatSessionStore's Sequencer. Provider refreshes retain the existing per-provider 500 ms ThrottledDelayer and parallelism across providers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: observeSession retains its per-resource guard, including failed attempts until refresh. Controller promises coalesce in-flight and successful/empty resolutions; controller failures remove their cache entry. Agent Merge configuration remains weakly cached per session/chat. Nested-chat counts still read catalog summaries, and hover Branch Changes are read only through the existing observed-data condition.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after renderer bodies, delegates, status helpers, and disposal methods match apart from exports and relocation; surrounding tree construction continues to pass the same dependencies and options.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large-history sizes, provider durations, and actual frame times are unmeasured. Existing expensive work is not evidence that this extraction amplifies it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Visibility gating, resolver frequency, header scans, DOM reconstruction, timers, and cleanup ownership are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open command-center sessions/blocked-sessions dropdowns and use approval or Fix CI actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsFlatList population and CommandCenterSessionsList height/layout calculation must finish before the dropdown paints. Height is bounded to eight base rows; content-height computation still visits the supplied sessions. CI/PR enrichment updates the existing reactive row presentation asynchronously. Fix CI submission remains background work triggered by an explicit click.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire shared live pull-request and CI models and refresh required-check/core data through the existing GitHub service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Concurrent references share models by owner/repository/PR number and, for CI, head SHA. Actual reads depend on live-model state, refresh, and subscription lifetime; they are not newly multiplied by every height read or template through this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical getCIFix delegate/renderer calls, shared reference keys, and delayed-store ownership; the model file changes only its interface import.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enrichment can delay availability of a CI row; the dropdown itself is not newly made to await network completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On Fix CI, build the prompt, acquire/load the selected chat session, and send its request through the existing chat backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One submission flow per explicitly selected session; _hiddenSessions guards duplicate clicks for that session until submission settles. Different selected sessions can submit independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same click handler, model implementation, duplicate-submit guard, awaits, and reference disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the dropdown's initial critical path; the row is optimistically hidden while background submission runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve lazy session properties for rendered dropdown rows using the shared agent-session model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Distinct rendered session resources after the shared per-resource guard/controller cache; dropdown scrolling exposes additional resources, not all sessions solely because they exist in the input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same flat-list renderer invocation and cached resolver path before extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous enrichment, not an awaited paint prerequisite.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Supplied blocked/preview sessions, their chats for aggregate approvals, distinct referenced PR/head keys, visible dropdown templates, and explicit user action count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Height/layout and approval rendering remain synchronous. Network/model work retains shared-key reference counting and per-model coalescing; independent keys can progress concurrently. Fix CI is guarded per session, not by a new global queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CI state observables remain weakly keyed by session; live PR/CI references are shared and delayedStore preserves them across recomputation. Per-model refresh promises still coalesce, and normal disposal/cancellation remains intact. Approval content/button stores are cleared on recompute and row recycling as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the import-only model/dropdown diffs, unchanged SessionsFlatList construction, and matching moved approval/CI renderer bodies.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency, pagination sizes, and number of blocked sessions are unknown; no changed cardinality or scheduling mechanism was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression introduced. Existing collection-height scans and GitHub/chat boundaries retain their frequency, sharing, lifecycle, and critical-path placement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display automation run history and update timestamps/status/approval rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Automation history builds its existing per-group SessionsFlatList instances, updates session inputs, computes full group content height, and lays out before display. Unlike the command-center dropdown, the history caller sets the list height to its full content height, so a group's rows can all render. The extraction does not change that cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve lazy properties of rendered history sessions through the existing session-item controller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the distinct rendered session resources across full-height history groups on a cold resolution epoch, reduced by the shared model/controller caches and unsupported-controller guard. Unchanged session arrays are rejected by the caller before setSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same per-group lists, full-height layout, identity-based update suppression, and resolver call in the formerly local renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution is not awaited by history layout; it supplies later row enrichment.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Runs/sessions in displayed history groups, distinct session resources, metadata/approval label sizes, and subsequent status/timestamp updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: List population, content-height reduction, width read, and layout are synchronous. Independent cold resolver requests can overlap; per-resource promises coalesce and metadata reads use the existing shared index sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Caller retains its identical session-array identity comparison and runsBySession mapping. Resolver caches are shared with other session surfaces. formatSessionListTime's body is unchanged; timestamp intervals remain 60 seconds with the same owning disposable stores. History explicitly disables rich session hovers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the sole importer change in automationRunHistory.ts, unchanged caller options/update/layout code, and matching renderer/time-helper implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History length and backend response times are unmeasured; any pre-existing cost of full-height history rendering was not introduced or amplified here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The import split preserves effective row count, timer lifetime, asynchronous backend fan-out, and synchronous layout work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 6a414e67387570378343d38583f4f19129dbe20e. Inspected all 14 changed files and all diff pages, comparing extracted declarations with their deleted originals and tracing relevant callers, resolution caches, metadata serialization, CI reference sharing, and row cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance finding or concrete regression-fix provenance signal qualified. Static review only; runtime/bundle timing was not measured.
